title: The two missing scores
prompt: Dylan's points were doubled and then 9 were taken away. The scorer wrote the resulting score twice, giving a total of 54. How many points did Dylan start with?

title: The opening bundle
prompt: A craft stall began with some ribbons. The first customer bought half the ribbons and 3 more. The second bought half of what remained and 2 more. Then the stallholder added 5 ribbons, leaving 12. How many ribbons were there at the start?

title: Find the variable part of a bill
prompt: A workshop charges $9 to enter and $4 per model built. A visitor pays $37. How many models did the visitor build?

title: The family ticket mix
prompt: A museum sells adult tickets for $9 and child tickets for $5. A group buys 11 tickets for $67. How many are adult tickets?

title: Find the weight of the box
prompt: A packed box weighs 29 kg. Its contents weigh 9 kg more than the empty box. How much does the empty box weigh, in kilograms?

title: Two ropes before the cut
prompt: Two ropes together measure 42 cm. After 8 cm is cut from the longer rope, it is still 6 cm longer than the shorter rope. How long was the shorter rope, in centimetres?

title: An extra pair of lamps
prompt: Two toolboxes and three lamps cost $45. Two of the same toolboxes and five lamps cost $59. How many dollars does one lamp cost?

title: Find the price by combining the bills
prompt: Two mugs and three bowls cost $37. Three mugs and two bowls cost $33. What is the cost of one mug and one bowl together, in dollars?

title: Undo a repeated doubling
prompt: Start with a whole number. Add 5 and then double. Repeat those two operations in the same order on the result. The final number is 54. What was the starting number?

title: One machine, two different endings
prompt: A machine doubles a number and adds 7. A second machine triples a number and subtracts 2. When the same whole number goes into both, their outputs are equal. What is the common output?

title: Change which bowl has more
prompt: One bowl has 50 beads and another has 30. How many beads must move from the first bowl to the second so that the second has 10 more than the first?

title: Keep the total, change the ratio
prompt: Two tanks contain 49 and 21 litres. Water is moved from the first to the second until the first has twice as much as the second. How many litres were moved? Give an exact fraction.

title: Two identical parcels
prompt: Two large parcels and one small parcel weigh 17 kg together. One large parcel and one small parcel weigh 11 kg together. All large parcels have equal weights and all small parcels have equal weights. How heavy is a small parcel, in kilograms?

title: The hidden gift bag
prompt: Three identical toy trains and one toy bus cost $36. Two trains and three buses cost $45. What is the cost of one train and one bus, in dollars?

title: Move a whole package
prompt: A shelf has 35 books and another has 17. Some books are moved from the first shelf to the second. Afterwards the shelves contain equal numbers. How many books are moved?

title: The second basket ends up with double
prompt: A basket has 38 apples and another has 16. Apples are moved from the first basket to the second until the second has twice as many as the first. How many apples are moved?

title: Before the two ribbon cuts
prompt: A ribbon is cut in half. From one half, 5 centimetres are removed. From the other half, 9 centimetres are removed. The two pieces left have a combined length of 28 centimetres. How long was the uncut ribbon, in centimetres?

title: Only one reversal produces a whole number
prompt: A machine triples a whole number and adds 4. One output label was smudged and could read 53, 54 or 55. Which output is possible?

title: Which offers cost the same?
prompt: At a fair, one ride pass costs $6 plus $2 per ride. Another costs $3 per ride with no joining fee. For how many rides do the passes cost the same?

title: A cinema with a free seat
prompt: A group of 12 people goes to the cinema. One child enters free. The other children's tickets are $6 each and adults' tickets are $9 each. The group pays $84. How many adults are in the group?

title: Three pair totals, one trip
prompt: Luca and Mira travel a total of 21 kilometres. Mira and Ned travel 25 kilometres. Luca and Ned travel 28 kilometres. How far does Ned travel, in kilometres?

title: A box of two kinds of token
prompt: A bag of 4 square tokens and 3 round tokens weighs 45 g. A bag of 5 square tokens and 2 round tokens weighs 44 g. Tokens of the same shape have equal weight. How heavy is one round token in grams?

title: An entrance price goes up
prompt: An activity charges a whole-dollar entry fee and $4 for each ride. A family takes five rides and pays $31. The next day the entry fee rises by $2, while rides still cost $4. What will the same number of rides cost the next day in dollars?

title: A tariff changes at five
prompt: A bike hire shop charges $5 for each of the first five hours and $3 for each hour after that. Caleb is charged $43 for a whole number of hours. How many hours did he hire the bike for?

title: Pass a few back
prompt: Eli has 26 counters and Dara has 14. Eli passes seven to Dara, and then Dara gives some back. Afterwards they have the same number. How many did Dara give back?

title: Add the transfer back
prompt: There are 80 beads in two bags. After 6 beads move from the larger bag to the smaller, both bags hold the same number. How many beads were in the larger bag before the move?

title: Undo the growth from the total
prompt: A shop has a whole number of seed packets. Each day for two days its stock triples and then it sells six packets. After day two there are 57 packets. How many packets were there before day one?

title: A three-stage scoring rule
prompt: A contest starts a team with an unknown whole number of points. At each of three stages it adds half the points the team has at that moment, then takes away six points. The team finishes with 39 points. How many points did it start with?

title: Pay by the bundle or one at a time
prompt: A shop sells pens for $3 each, or a pack of five for $12. What is the smallest number of dollars needed to buy exactly 13 pens?

title: Count the notes in the box
prompt: A cashbox contains 14 notes worth $5, $10 or $20 each. Exactly two are $20 notes. The total is $135. How many are $10 notes?

title: Two bags and one spill
prompt: Two bags together hold 52 marbles. The heavier bag loses 6 marbles through a hole, so that the two bags now hold equal numbers. How many marbles were originally in the heavier bag?

title: All three bowls end equal
prompt: Three bowls hold 8, 17 and 29 counters. You can move one counter at a time from any bowl to another. What is the smallest number of moves that makes all three bowls hold equal numbers?

title: Compare two dinner orders
prompt: One table orders three soups and two drinks for $31. Another orders one soup and two drinks for $17. What does one soup and one drink cost in dollars?

title: The price of the missing fruit
prompt: An apple, a pear and a plum cost $13 altogether. Two apples and one pear cost $14. Two pears and one plum cost $15. How many dollars does a pear cost?

title: The lesson that pays a hire fee
prompt: A lesson room costs $48 to hire, then $3 for each pupil. The bill must be paid in full from ticket money. Each pupil pays $7. What is the least number of pupils needed?

title: Combine two trips on one ferry
prompt: A ferry ticket for a bicycle and rider costs $9. A walking rider's ticket costs $5. Two groups together contain 18 riders. The first group has six bicycles. The second group has two more walking riders than bicycles. Together the groups pay $130. How many riders are in the second group?

title: A transfer changes the winner
prompt: Nora has 45 beads and Suri has 25. Nora gives Suri enough to make Suri's collection 8 larger than Nora's. How many beads does Nora give?

title: A smaller store gives away more
prompt: A large store and a small store together have 73 boxes. After the small store receives five boxes from a delivery and sends eight of its boxes to the large store, the large store has twice as many boxes as the small one. How many did the small store have at the start?

title: Square and subtract twice
prompt: A machine squares any number entered and then subtracts 7. A positive whole number is put in, and its output is fed into the machine again. The second output is 74. What was the first number entered?

title: Read the machine in the other direction
prompt: The same whole number is used in two calculations. First double it, subtract 5, and multiply the result by 3. Next multiply the original number by 5 and add 2. The first result is 11 greater than the second. What was the original number?

title: Balance the hidden bag
prompt: Four equal green bags and two equal gold bags weigh 38 kg. Three green bags and two gold bags weigh 31 kg. What is the weight of one green bag and one gold bag together, in kilograms?

title: Red packets in place of blue packets
prompt: Three red packets and two blue packets weigh 48 g. Three red packets and five blue packets weigh 84 g. Packets of the same colour have equal weights. How many red packets weigh the same as six blue packets?
